result.summary: Do not dispatch: the specified discovery can make an existing integration test delete real scheduler files.

findings.title: Isolate the integration test's XDG scheduler root before widening deletion
findings.body: D1 enumerates every scheduler root, but tests/integration/uninstall-core-e2e.test.js inherits XDG_CONFIG_HOME while redirecting HOME. Read-only execution of its environment builder confirmed systemdUserDir still resolves outside the sandbox. With a real wienerdog-personal-routine.timer there, discovery would include it and R4 would delete it because the fixture manifest does not record it. The test grants deletion clearance; WIENERDOG_LOADER_NOOP suppresses scheduler commands, not filesystem deletion. Thus npm test could remove the developer's real timer/service files. The affected integration test is also absent from the Deliverables table.
findings.recommendation: Add the integration test to Deliverables and require its XDG_CONFIG_HOME to point inside the temporary HOME. Add a regression using a simulated external XDG root that verifies its schedule files survive the sandboxed uninstall, and audit other discovery callers for inherited scheduler roots.

next_steps: Amend the isolation requirements and permitted files, then rerun the design review.
